Edges only ever run between the rows." width="100%"} Creates `n1` nodes in a first part and `n2` in a second, and picks `m` of the `n1 * n2` pairs across the parts uniformly at random, with no repeats, so every bipartite graph on these parts with `m` edges is equally likely. If `m` is at least `n1 * n2`, every pair is joined, giving the complete bipartite graph. This is the bipartite version of `add_gnm_graph()` and NetworkX's `bipartite.gnmk_random_graph()`. NetworkX returns no edges at all when either part has a single node; here those cases get their `m` edges too. Each node's part is stored in the `part_attr=` node attribute (`0` for the first, `1` for the second). The first part is created first, and in a directed graph every edge points from the first part to the second. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random bipartite graphs with a fixed edge count are useful for: - null models for two-mode networks that keep the exact number of edges - benchmarking bipartite algorithms at a controlled size - comparing an observed bipartite network with random ones of the same density ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the first part. Must be non-negative. [n2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the second part. Must be non-negative. [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of edges. Must be non-negative; values above `n1 * n2` are capped there. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. [part_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["part"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's part (`0` or `1`). Default is `"part"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n1=`, `n2=` or `m=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Ten edges between a part of four nodes and a part of five: ::: {#698b9245 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_bipartite_gnm_graph(4, 5, m=10, seed=1) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), graph.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (9, 10, True) ``` ::: ::: Asking for more edges than there are pairs gives the complete bipartite graph: ::: {#a5b53a7f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_bipartite_gnm_graph(4, 5, m=100).count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 20 ``` ::: :::
